Hi Laura —

Thanks again for last week's demo. Our procurement team asked for one more clarification ahead of the pricing review on Monday. Specifically: how do you account for tokens when we rely heavily on long context windows across replies (avg. prompt 5–7k tokens, sometimes up to 32k)? Two related items:

- If we reuse prefixes across many requests (same customer history), does Redwood count those tokens every call or is there an amortization/credit?
- We need an example invoice line where small micro-calls (1–3 short API calls) happen in a session that also has a long-history call — how are minimums and rounding handled?

Also, FinWave is evaluating a 12‑month committed volume. We want to model concessions: would a time-phased discount (larger discounts after month 3 based on utilization) be possible, or do you prefer a flat commit discount?

I attached a short worksheet of our expected call mix. Would be great if you can respond with a short, architect-style walkthrough we can share internally.

Best,

Hi Ella —

Thanks — helpful worksheet. I put together a concise architectural walkthrough below (pasted to help your procurement and finance folks):

1) Token lifecycle and prefix reuse
- Per-request accounting: Redwood meters the literal tokens submitted and generated per API call by default.
- Prefix/KV cache credits: When a prefix (conversation history) is served from a hot KV cache without recomputing embeddings or re-encoding, we apply prefix reuse crediting. Practically this means repeated requests that entirely reuse cached KV entries are discounted via an amortization factor (we show this in the example invoice).
- Policy detail: credits kick in when more than 60% of model context is satisfied from cached KV state for three or more consecutive calls. Credits are applied at invoice time as a negative line item referencing the prefix_key.

2) Long-context calls + micro-calls in same session (rounding/minimums)
- Minimums: we have a per-session minimum charge that ensures very small bursts are not over-penalized. Example: session minimum = 8 token-units for a 1–3 micro-call burst.
- Rounding: token usage is quantized to the configured billing quantum (e.g., 100 token unit increments) for each call, but we roll up all calls in a session and apply a post-rollup floor (the session minimum) before finalizing the invoice line.
- Invoice mapping: micro-calls are listed as separate items but a session-level rollup line shows the applied minimum/floor with the distributed credit.

3) Example (from your worksheet, simplified)
- Call A: short prompt (120 tokens) -> billed at 100 quantum = 100 tokens
- Call B: long-history request (6,400 tokens) with 4,500 tokens satisfied from KV cache -> billed tokens = 1,900 (6,400 minus amortized cached portion) -> rounded to quantum = 1,900
- Session rollup: total raw billed = 2,000 tokens -> apply session minimum (8 token-units) and no change since above minimum -> final billed = 2,000 tokens
- Credit line: prefix reuse amortization shown as -4,500 tokens credit at conversion rate -> invoice shows both raw and net.

4) Commit/discount structure options
- Flat commit: single discount on per-token rate across duration. Simpler for invoicing and forecasting.
- Time-phased: we can support a stepped discount schedule tied to utilization windows (e.g., 10% months 1–3, 18% months 4–12) but it requires a utilization reporting clause and monthly reconciliation. We typically add a utilization true-up at months 3 and 12.
- Recommendation: for your expected ramp, a hybrid works best — modest flat commit discount + utilization-triggered bonus. That minimizes reconciliation friction.

5) Next steps
- Attached is a sample pricing matrix and a redlineable SOW (we can generate a one-page summary for procurement).
- Karthik and Ben are looped for uplift math and a sample invoice.

Happy to hop on a 30-minute call if you want us to walk the procurement team through the worksheet live.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett | Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference

Quick internal note (copying back to Ella to keep procurement aligned):

Laura — nice high-level. For the sample invoice I'll propose two concrete templates for FinWave:

A) Conservative: flat 15% commit discount; prefix credits applied as negative invoice lines; session minimums enforced exactly as Laura described. No monthly true-up, annual true-up only.

B) Ramp + utilization: 10% months 1–2, 18% months 3–12 if utilization > 70% of committed tokens. Monthly utilization reporting required; monthly true-up with cap. Also offer one-time onboarding credit to cover early prefix warm-up (to smooth month 1 charges).

Notes for the invoice example I'll attach: explicit mapping from API call -> billed token quantum -> prefix amortization -> human-readable line (e.g., "Prefix reuse credit (cust_123): -4,500 tokens -> -$45.00"). Ben, can you double-check the $/token numbers and attach a sample line?

-Karthik
